items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we have the following arithmetic sequence with first term [MATH: a_1 = {\color{red}4}] and common difference [MATH: d={\color{blue}{3}}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}{4}},7,10,13,16,\ldots]

Content:
Each term is [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] more than the previous, starting with [MATH: {\color{red}{4}}.] Therefore, we can express this sequence recursively:

Content:
[MATH: a_{n+1} = a_n + {\color{blue}{3}}, \quad a_1 = {\color{red}{4}}, \quad n\geq 1]

Content:
We can also express the sequence using function notation:

Content:
[MATH: f(n+1) = f(n) + {\color{blue}{3}}, \quad f(1) = {\color{red}{4}}, \quad n\geq 1]

items.title: Computing the Terms of an Arithmetic Sequence

sections.normalized_html:
Calculate the fourth term of the sequence

[MATH: f(n+1) = f(n) -6, \quad f(1) = 1, \quad n\geq 1.]
sections.readable_text:
Calculate the fourth term of the sequence

[MATH: f(n+1) = f(n) -6, \quad f(1) = 1, \quad n\geq 1.]

sections.normalized_html:
Starting with the first term [MATH: f(1)=1,] we compute the next terms using the recursive rule until we reach the fourth term [MATH: f(4).]

[MATH: f(1)|= 1; f(2)|= f(1) − 6 = 1 − 6 = − 5; f(3)|= f(2) − 6 = − 5 − 6 = − 11; f(4)|= f(3) − 6 = − 11 − 6 = − 17]

Therefore, the fourth term is [MATH: f(4)=-17.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose we have the following arithmetic sequence with first term [MATH: a_1 = {\color{red}4}] and common difference [MATH: d={\color{blue}{3}}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}{4}},7,10,13,16,\ldots]

Content:
Each term is [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] more than the previous, starting with [MATH: {\color{red}{4}}.] Therefore, we can express this sequence recursively:

Content:
[MATH: a_{n+1} = a_n + {\color{blue}{3}}, \quad a_1 = {\color{red}{4}}, \quad n\geq 1]

Content:
We can also express the sequence using function notation:

Content:
[MATH: f(n+1) = f(n) + {\color{blue}{3}}, \quad f(1) = {\color{red}{4}}, \quad n\geq 1]

---

Item 2 — Example: Computing the Terms of an Arithmetic Sequence

Example Prompt:
Calculate the fourth term of the sequence

[MATH: f(n+1) = f(n) -6, \quad f(1) = 1, \quad n\geq 1.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Starting with the first term [MATH: f(1)=1,] we compute the next terms using the recursive rule until we reach the fourth term [MATH: f(4).]

[MATH: f(1)|= 1; f(2)|= f(1) − 6 = 1 − 6 = − 5; f(3)|= f(2) − 6 = − 5 − 6 = − 11; f(4)|= f(3) − 6 = − 11 − 6 = − 17]

Therefore, the fourth term is [MATH: f(4)=-17.]

---

Item 5 — Example: Finding a Recursive Formula

Example Prompt:
What is the recursive formula for the following arithmetic sequence?
[MATH: 4,\: 9,\: 14,\: \ldots]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence with common difference [MATH: d] is

[MATH: a_{n+1} =a_n+d.]

In our case, the common difference is

[MATH: d|= a_{2} − a_{1}; = 9 − 4; = 5.]

Consequently, the recursive formula for this sequence is

[MATH: a_{n+1}= a_n + 5, \quad a_1=4, \quad n\geq 1\,.]
